message.content:
This looks like a CBP ruling on disposable underwear made of nonwoven fabric. Disposable underwear of nonwovens is typically classified in 6108.21 (women's briefs, knitted or crocheted) or 6208.91 (nonwoven?) — but nonwoven garments fall under 6210 ("garments made up of fabrics of heading 5602, 5603, 5903, 5906 or 5907"). Nonwoven spun bond laminated with paper pulp is in heading 5603 (nonwovens, laminated). Heading 6210 covers garments made of 5603 fabrics, but 6210 is for garments not elsewhere specified; underwear made of nonwovens is generally classified in 6212 or 6210? Past rulings on disposable nonwoven underwear classify in 6307.90 or 6212? I recall disposable underwear of nonwoven classified in 6210.50 (other women's garments). Subheading 6210.50 has 6210.50.2000 (Women's or girls' other garments, of man-made fibers?). Actually 6210.50.20 is "Other women's or girls' garments: of cotton"? Specifically: 6210.50.20 = "Other garments, women's: Of wool or fine animal hair"? I believe 6210.50.2000 is "Other women's or girls' garments: Other", HTS 6210.50.2000 being "Of man-made fibers"? Going with 6210.50.9060 is uncertain; I'll select 6210.50.2000.

{"hts_code": "6210.50.2000", "reason": "The disposable briefs are made of laminated nonwoven fabric of heading 5603, so they are classified as women's garments of heading 6210, under 6210.50 for other women's garments."}
